tasks.notes: plan-defect: the Global Constraint "unref every setTimeout the backoff creates" (echoed by the Context slot: "The backoff is a `setTimeout` promise with `unref()` so a sim never holds the process open") cannot be satisfied by a correct engine, and the submission knowingly diverges. `infraSleep` (fleet/run-engine.mjs, the `const infraSleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, ms) })` line) creates a ref'd timer, and the 11-line comment above it discloses exactly why: node exits the moment only unref'd handles remain, so an AWAITED unref'd timer is dropped — `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0).unref())` exits 13 with "unsettled top-level await". Every one of the three wait sites is a point where this promise can be the only pending work (the critic runs alone at its barrier per run-engine.mjs:2724; a wave's last reviewer is its wave's last call), so unref'ing would end the RUN, not the wait. The property the constraint protects is bought by construction instead: exactly one timer per re-dispatch, always awaited, at most one re-dispatch per judgment, and a fired timer holds nothing. I take the constraint to require that no engine timer outlive the work it gates — that holds here. Graded minor rather than blocking because the divergence is correct and disclosed, and the fix lies in the plan's own constraint text, outside this task's FILES. Constraint carries no `Check:`, so this rests on my reading of prose; recorded for the operator.; The committed sim asserts the opposite of what the engine does, in a comment. fleet/tests/test_run_engine_infra_retry.mjs opens its heartbeat block with "The backoff's own timer is `unref`'d (a Global Constraint of this task: no timer of the engine's holds the process open) ... Without it a correct engine would end the sim mid-await with exit 13." The engine's timer is NOT unref'd — run-engine.mjs's own comment says so at length and explains why — so the stated rationale for `const heartbeat = setInterval(() => {}, 100)` is false and the heartbeat is dead scaffolding: with a ref'd timer the loop is alive regardless. Nothing fails today (the interval is cleared before the sentinel and a green run still exits 0), but the next reader is told the engine unrefs when it deliberately does not, which is the one fact about this backoff a future edit is most likely to get wrong. Fix inside FILES: correct the comment to name the disclosed divergence, and either drop the heartbeat or keep it explicitly as a guard against a future unref.; Two paths outside the declared FILES are edited — fleet/tests/test_run_engine_exam_together.mjs and fleet/tests/test_run_engine_examiner.mjs (the driver's footprint arithmetic names both).
